text:
Maya: FYI I'm hitting a weird resolve error when running the sample-app in the Edge runtime locally (pnpm workspace). Works in node dev, fails in edge build.

Maya: Error: Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './dist/esm' is not defined by "exports" in /workspace/packages/sdk/package.json

Maya: stack: 
```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './dist/esm' is not defined by "exports" in /workspace/packages/sdk/package.json
    at throwExportsNotFound (internal/modules/esm/resolve.js:...)
    at packageExportsResolve (internal/modules/esm/resolve.js:...)
    at defaultResolve (internal/modules/esm/resolve.js:...)
```

Liam: :eyes: Are you importing a deep path like `@redwood/sdk/dist/esm`? Edge runtimes (esbuild/bun/deno-like) treat package exports strictly.

Maya: Yeah the sample-app does `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk/dist/esm'` because we wanted the ESM entry for edge. In the monorepo that path exists via pnpm symlink but the package.json only has a limited `exports` map.

Chris: Long story short: workspace symlinks + exports + ESM = surprise. Node resolves symlinked packages differently and the Edge bundler complains if the subpath isn't exported.

Aisha: Two common fixes: 1) update package `exports` to include the subpath, or 2) stop importing deep paths and use the public entrypoints we declare (e.g. `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`). First option is fragile but sometimes necessary for the sample.

Liam: Example exports snippet that would fix this:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./dist/esm": "./dist/esm/index.js"
}
```

Maya: I can add that, but I worry about leaking internal build paths. Also this doesn't fix the pnpm hoisting/symlink behavior where the bundler resolves the package root differently during CI.

Chris: For CI and local parity, try `node --preserve-symlinks` for Node-based builds, or better: avoid relying on symlinked internal paths in the sample. For pnpm, `pnpm install --shamefully-hoist` is an option but not great.

Aisha: Another pattern: publish a small `@redwood/sdk-edge` entry that is ESM-only and explicitly meant for bundlers/edge. The sample app can depend on that in workspace so there's a clear exported entry. It separates edge surface from node surface.

Maya: Noted. Short-term I'm going to update the sample to use the public entry and add a note in onboarding docs about not importing `./dist` deep paths. Will open a tiny PR to change sample imports and adjust package exports so CI Edge builds are happy.

Liam: Also add a test in the sample CI job to `esbuild --bundle` the app (or run the actual edge build) so we catch this earlier.

Maya: Will do. Opening PR in a bit.

deps-bot: Automated note: workspace packages changed: packages/sdk/package.json (exports)

Chris: tiny follow-up — for TypeScript users, make sure `types`/`exports` align (TS path mapping can mask problems). We had one case where `types` pointed at `./dist/index.d.ts` but runtime import mapped to `./dist/esm/index.js`, bundler still failed because `./dist/esm` wasn't exported.

Aisha: Good call. Add a line in the DX checklist: "verify edge bundle + types resolution in workspace".

Maya: Thanks all — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/123 (fix imports + docs). :party:
